info.title: API.SH: Skyscanner
info.description: The Skyscanner API from API.SH: public Skyscanner data as clean JSON. Every endpoint is a GET with query parameters and your key in the x-api-key header. Calls that run cost the credits shown (x-credits): successes, and lookups that found nothing (404). Refused calls and errors on our side are free. Docs: https://api.sh/docs · Every platform: https://api.sh/openapi.json

get.description:
Places matching a few letters, as Skyscanner's search boxes suggest them. type=flight: airports, cities and countries with Skyscanner code, IATA code, entity id, city, country and coordinates (the codes and ids the flight routes take). type=hotel: cities, districts and points of interest with entity ids for /skyscanner/v1/hotels.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/skyscanner-autocomplete

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: A few letters of a place name or code.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Rental car quotes for a pick-up place and time: car model, ACRISS (SIPP) code, price, supplier and its rating, booking site, pick-up type, seats, bags, air conditioning, transmission, fuel policy, mileage and free cancellation, with booking links. Results come in car groups (one model from one supplier with its booking-site quotes); `total` counts groups. Pass `next_offset` back as `offset`; it is null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/skyscanner-car-hire

parameters.name: pickup
parameters.description: Pick-up airport or city code, entity id or city name.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: recommended (default), price (cheapest first) or distance (nearest pick-up first).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Skyscanner's "Everywhere" search: the cheapest flights from an origin to every country (and featured cities), with the cheapest price, whether it is direct, the cheapest direct price and an image, plus the site's themed lists (cheapest, direct, popular, beach, food, nightlife...). For a month, a date or any time; optional return.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/skyscanner-everywhere

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: Departure airport or city code, entity id or city name.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Departure date YYYY-MM-DD instead of a month.

parameters.name: return_month
parameters.description: Return month YYYY-MM for round trips.

parameters.name: return_date
parameters.description: Return date YYYY-MM-DD for round trips.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.summary: Skyscanner cheapest flight prices by day
get.description:
The cheapest one-way price for each departure day between two places. With `month`: every day of that month with the cheapest direct and indirect price and, for each, the airports, airline, booking site and when the price was found. Without `month`: the cheapest price and price level (low, medium, high) for every day of the year ahead.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/skyscanner-flight-calendar

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: Departure airport or city code, entity id or city name.

parameters.name: destination
parameters.description: Arrival airport or city code, entity id or city name.

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: YYYY-MM for one month in detail (default: the year ahead).

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Flight search on Skyscanner, one-way or return: every itinerary the search finds, with price, the booking sites and their prices with booking links, legs (airports, departure and arrival times, duration, stops, airlines, operating airline) and each segment's flight number, self-transfer flag, fare change/refund policy and CO2 estimate. Filter by the most stops per leg, airlines and a price ceiling; sort by best, cheapest, fastest or departure time. `filter_stats` has the cheapest price by number of stops and by airline, and the booking sites with their ratings. Places are airport or city codes (JFK, NYC, LON), Skyscanner entity ids or city names. Each search answers a `search_id` (kept as long as the search's cached answer, see `search_expires_at`): pass it with `next_offset` as `offset` and every page comes from that same search, with the same prices, and returns at once; other sorts and filters work on it too. `next_offset` is null on the last page. If a call times out, ask again with the same parameters: you get that same search (still running, or finished in the last 2 minutes) instead of a new one. Every booking-site offer has `quote_time`, when the booking site's price was taken (UTC), and `quote_age_minutes`; prices of popular routes are often several minutes to a few hours old at the source, so filter on `quote_age_minutes` when you need recent ones.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/skyscanner-flights

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description: Departure airport or city: code (JFK, NYC), Skyscanner entity id or city name.

parameters.name: destination
parameters.description: Arrival airport or city: code (LHR, LON), entity id or city name.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Departure date YYYY-MM-DD (default: 30 days from today).

parameters.name: return_date
parameters.description: Return date YYYY-MM-DD for a round trip (default: one-way).

parameters.name: stops
parameters.description: Most stops per leg: direct, 1 or 2 (default any).

parameters.name: airlines
parameters.description: Only these airlines (two-letter codes, comma separated, e.g. BA,AA).

parameters.name: market
parameters.description: Market country (default US): sets prices and availability, e.g. UK, DE, IN.

parameters.name: currency
parameters.description: Price currency (default USD; GBP for market UK).

parameters.name: search_id
parameters.description: `search_id` from the first page: later pages, sorts and filters read that same search (until `search_expires_at`; 410 when expired: search again with `fresh=1`). The search parameters are then not needed.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

get.description:
Hotels for a city or area and dates: name, stars, area, guest rating and review count, cheapest price per night or for the stay (before discount, with taxes, discount percent), photos, the booking sites' offers with prices and links, and the hotel page link. `total` is the number of hotels found; `median_price` the median cheapest price. Pass `next_offset` back as `offset`; it is null on the last page.

Every response includes `credits_used`: the credits this call cost.

Price: 1 credit per successful call. Docs: https://api.sh/docs/skyscanner-hotels

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: City or area name (or pass entity_id).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: best (default), price, rating, stars or distance.

200.description: The data as JSON (or CSV / NDJSON with `output`).

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Create keys at https://app.api.sh/keys. Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.

raw.name: raw
raw.description: 0 leaves out the bulky `raw` source blocks (often 10-30x smaller).

fields.name: fields
fields.description: Comma-separated fields to return, e.g. `posts.id,posts.title`. Call metadata is always included.

fresh.name: fresh
fresh.description: 1 skips the 24-hour cache and fetches live.

output.name: output
output.description: csv or ndjson returns the response's records (its main list, or the object as one row) as CSV or NDJSON instead of JSON.

records.name: records
records.description: With output=csv|ndjson: the top-level list to turn into rows (e.g. `reviews`), or `.` for the whole object as one row.

status_url.description: On a 503 for a paused endpoint: the status page, which lists open incidents.

E400.description: A parameter is missing or invalid. Not charged (unless the call ran and the source rejected the value; credits_used says).

E401.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired API key. Not charged. See https://api.sh/docs/errors#401

E402.description: Not enough credits, a spend limit you set was reached (`spend_limit`), or the key's monthly credit cap was reached (`key_cap`). Not charged.

E404.description: Not found, or not public. A lookup that ran costs the endpoint's price (credits_used says); an unknown route is free.

E502.description: The source site failed this time; retry. Not charged.

E503.description: Endpoint paused or temporarily unavailable; may include retry-after, and status_url (https://api.sh/status) for a paused endpoint. Not charged.
